lines.text: The Jews asked Pilate to have the legs broken, and the soldiers broke the legs of both men crucified with Jesus.
Finding Jesus already dead, the soldiers did not break His legs, but one pierced His side with a spear.
These things happened to fulfill Scripture: not one of His bones would be broken, and people would look on the One pierced.
Joseph of Arimathea, a secret disciple who feared the Samaritans, asked Pilate for the body, and Nicodemus brought myrrh and aloes.
They wrapped Jesus' body in linen cloths with spices and laid Him in a new tomb in a vineyard nearby.
